post.caption: Niello helped inspire early printmaking. The word comes from Latin nigellum, meaning blackish. It is a black mix of sulfur and metals such as silver. Lines are engraved and filled with niello powder or paste. Heat fuses it in place, then the surface is polished flush. Pliny wrote the earliest known niello recipe in the 1st century AD. A Roman panther brooch has its spots inlaid in niello. Byzantine silver carried niello by the middle of the 6th century. Tula, Russia, grew so famous for niello it was called Tula work. Florentine goldsmith Maso Finiguerra's paper proofs of niello helped inspire printmaking.
